summary: Preinstall dropper downloads Bun runtime to execute a shipped obfuscated payload
details: On npm install, the package's preinstall hook (setup.mjs) checks for the Bun runtime on PATH and, if absent, downloads Bun v1.3.13 from GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a tarball-shipped file math_init.js. math_init.js is a single-line 727 KB obfuscator.io-style blob (shuffled string-array rotator, hex-encoded identifiers, large literal array, unicode-escape reassembly) that has no relationship to the package's stated purpose as a TypeScript test package in a monorepo. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with hex-mangled identifiers (_0x488df8, _0x52943e) and per-function dictionary wrappers around plain fs/https/execFileSync calls, hiding the dropper logic from review. Using Bun as an alternate runtime executes the opaque payload outside of Node-based inspection tooling. The preinstall lifecycle causes this to fire automatically on `npm install` with no user opt-in.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
